clue.text: Black bishop installed in Cheshire town

indicators.note: something installed in a place is put inside it, so the bishop goes within the town

parts.note: Sale is a town in Cheshire, near Manchester
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A dark-clad cleric takes up a post in a northern English town.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the colour black is called by this name, as is the dark fur.

clue.text: Substantiate smelly condition in outskirts of Selby

indicators.note: one group of letters sits inside the edges of the town's name
outskirts are the edge of a town, so only the first and last letters of the name are used

parts.note: olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: Someone confirms a report of a nasty smell on the edge of a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Selby is a town in North Yorkshire. 'Olid' is a rare word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: To make firm or concrete; substantiating a claim is firming it up, a looser synonym.

clue.text: Butler's developing swagger

indicators.note: something developing changes its form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A servant is growing a self-important manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the S of 'Butler's' is part of the letters to rearrange, not a possessive to ignore.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe loud, boastful, arrogant behaviour meant to impress or intimidate.

clue.text: Headless toy found in swirling water

indicators.note: without its head, the first letter of the word is taken off

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A decapitated plaything is discovered floating in a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: A small whirlpool or circular current in a river is the standard sense.

clue.text: Transfer Duke inside royal house

indicators.note: one letter is placed within the name of the dynasty

parts.note: Hanover was the German royal house that ruled Britain from George I to Victoria

explanation.surface: A duke takes up residence in a palace belonging to the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for passing over control or responsibility, as in a shift handover.

clue.text: Chief, reasoning correctly, preserves most of vast age. It's all to do with excavation

definitions.text: It's all to do with excavation

indicators.note: to preserve is to keep safely within, so the age sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: arch means chief, as in arch-enemy
logical means reasoning soundly

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: an aeon is an immensely long age

explanation.surface: A logical leader keeps ancient remains intact; the topic is digging.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the study of the past through digging up sites and objects.

clue.text: Mounting anger leads to ruin

indicators.note: in a down clue, something mounting rises, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a mood is a fit of bad temper, as in 'in a mood'

explanation.surface: Rising fury ends in destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a terrible fate or destruction awaiting someone.

clue.text: Essentially event is about game

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letters are kept

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: The heart of the occasion is all about sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of EVENT is VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means wild animals hunted for food; deer meat is one such.

clue.text: In the end Caesar's fateful day oppresses

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: A historical note on how Caesar's fatal day finally weighed on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of CAESAR is R, then IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride someone is to harass or dominate them, as in riding roughshod.

clue.text: Relatives at beginning of disaster shrug danger off

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong, as in milk gone off, so the letters are scrambled
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: At the first sign of calamity, people brush peril aside.
explanation.walkthrough: AT, D from 'disaster' and SHRUGDANGER are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandparent's female grandchildren are relatives, an example of the class.

clue.text: Clean district surrounding university before Queen's arrival

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, so the area encloses the letter

parts.note: land can mean a region or district
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An area around a college is tidied up before a royal visit.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash clothes, or to make dirty money look legitimate; both are senses of cleaning.

clue.text: Around middle of Stone Age lots of people got hit on the head

indicators.note: the gathering of people goes round the central letters

parts.note: a crowd is a large group of people

indicators.note: the middle of the phrase is its central two letters

explanation.surface: In prehistoric times, many people were clubbed over the head.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of STONEAGE is NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to be struck on the head is to be crowned, a slang sense.

clue.text: Son avoids dull service

indicators.note: the letter for son keeps away from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: dusty means dry and dull
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy dodges tedious obligations.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour of duty is a period of service; both mean work one is obliged to do.

clue.text: Massage joint's said to lie at end of road

indicators.note: said signals that a word is spoken and written as a same-sounding spelling

parts.note: the knee is a joint; 's is short for is

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sore joint gets rubbed, said to lie at the end of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is pronounced like KNEE plus D, so the joint word is heard and the D from 'road' lies after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To work dough or muscles with the hands is a kind of massage.

clue.text: Heart of Lancashire is unaltered

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: The centre of a northern county remains unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of LANCASHIRE are AS. Lancashire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold in its present condition, without changes, is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Roll sack over railroad in Chicago

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: a bag is a sack
the El is Chicago's elevated railway

explanation.surface: A bag is slung over an American train line.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked, is this item.

clue.text: Former Tsarist edict from this country's a hollow statute

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, the setter's country; 's is short for is

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Something from Britain is an empty law, like an old Russian decree.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by the Russian tsar or government was given this name.

clue.text: Progressive in favour of adjusting work load in Government

parts.note: for means supporting

indicators.note: adjusting changes the arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Supporting changes to how much work civil servants do.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone progressive plans for the future, the core sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Adam's first son, ultimately jealous, sadly is not quite sane. He's a killer

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the name

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter
sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters are muddled
not quite the whole word means the last letter is lost

explanation.surface: Adam's jealous son Cain was mad, and became the first murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: IS and SAN are rearranged into ASSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer, especially one who kills a prominent person, is described as a killer.

clue.text: Being ingratiating former pupil, forgetting time and name, excitedly questions upper-class head

parts.note: OB stands for Old Boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: excitedly suggests agitation, so the letters are mixed up
forgetting leaves something out, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: An old boy, absent-minded, eagerly quizzes the posh headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: QUESTIONS without T and N leaves QUESIOS; with U it is rearranged into SEQUIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive eagerness to please or obey is the noun's meaning, matching ingratiating behaviour.

clue.text: Heckle President's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Barack Obama was a US President

explanation.surface: Someone jeers at a presidential television address.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain and Australia, to jeer at a speaker or player is to barrack them.

clue.text: European omitting introduction to Attlee's first principle

indicators.note: omitting the introduction means the first letter is left off

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the UK Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951; his first name

explanation.surface: A European leaves out the start of a postwar Prime Minister's main policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic part or rudiment of a subject is a principle, as in elements of geometry.

clue.text: Flood's a nuisance

definitions.meaning: a tidal wave surging up a river, as on the Severn, is a sudden flood

explanation.surface: Complaining that high water is a pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge up an estuary is one sense; a tiresome person or thing the other.

clue.text: The sort of pal to hug to one's chest

definitions.meaning: an intimate friend is described as a close pal of this kind
to embrace or clasp someone close

explanation.surface: A close friend is the kind you embrace warmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A very close friend is a bosom pal; as a verb the word means to embrace.

clue.text: Chinese own Scottish links

parts.note: ain is the Scots word for own

explanation.surface: Asian owners of Scottish golf courses.
explanation.walkthrough: Links are seaside golf courses, common in Scotland, which is the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of connected links forms the whole; here links means the rings themselves.

clue.text: Fellow regularly eats American cheese

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A man routinely eats cheese from the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: A white Greek cheese made from sheep or goat milk is an example.

clue.text: In Paris you run fine horse-racing

parts.note: tu is French for you
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A French speaker tells you that you run well at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: The turf is a collective term for horse-racing, from the grass courses.

clue.text: Steal Conservative's wife

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
Eve was made from Adam's rib, so rib is jocular for a wife

explanation.surface: Pinching a Tory politician's spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone else's work, or to pilfer, is informal cribbing.

clue.text: Carved figure is about right height

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the figure wraps round the letter

parts.note: a statue is a carved figure

explanation.surface: A sculpture is roughly the right size.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's natural standing height, or figuratively importance, is this noun.

clue.text: Stuffy Earl is a touch superior in a funny sort of way

indicators.text: in a funny sort of way
indicators.note: funny means odd, so these letters are put in an odd order
a touch of a word is only its first letter

explanation.surface: A haughty nobleman is somewhat superior, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: EARLIS with S from 'superior' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuffy room lacks fresh air, the literal sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Secure fake nuts among acorns

indicators.note: among means amid, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: mast is the fallen fruit of oak and beech trees, such as acorns

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Hiding counterfeit nuts within a pile of acorns.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical phrase for tying up or fastening a boat or rope.

clue.text: Carry on playing with stick

definitions.meaning: in cricket, to keep batting is to continue at the crease
a short rod, as used by a conductor or relay runner

explanation.surface: Keep going with a stick in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means keep batting; as one it is a rod or stick.
